claims.statement: Organization access is through the person's signed-in account, not a separate organization login. The resolved navigation uses the profile Organizations menu then selects the organization; navigating successfully does not prove access to every organization resource.
The guide says only organization owners can see and change organization account settings. Membership, a public organization avatar or existence of a settings URL is not proof of owner authority.

The organization-membership index covers FPT/GHES/GHEC and links six procedures: organization access, roles, OAuth requests, membership visibility, organization departure and enterprise departure. Child product and actor scopes are narrower than the navigation metadata.

Across FPT/GHES/GHEC, membership visibility is changed from the selected organization's People list by locating one's username and choosing Public or Private in the visibility dropdown. This changes displayed membership, not membership status or resource authorization.

The guide concerns showing organization avatars on one's profile. Hiding membership is not a guarantee of anonymity, removal from the organization or loss of organization access; no live visibility change or observer test occurs here.

This enterprise-leave guide is FPT/GHEC, not GHES. Personal-account members may leave, while enterprise managed users can only be removed by administrators; username suffix and enterprise domain examples are identification clues rather than sufficient verified account-type evidence.

After departure, organization membership and enterprise-granted Copilot licenses and other privileges are lost. These effects require approved access, ownership, workflow and entitlement-impact review, not an instruction to execute removal.

The personal-account sequence first leaves every enterprise organization using the Your role filter, then rechecks the Enterprises settings page. If the enterprise is absent, the source describes departure; missing API permission or an incomplete collector list must not be mistaken for this authenticated UI observation.

If still listed, an unaffiliated member uses Leave; an owner must remove themself in enterprise settings; a billing manager asks an enterprise owner to remove them. These role-specific procedures and linked administrator instructions are not interchangeable or authority grants.

The guide describes members and outside collaborators leaving an organization through Settings, Access, Organizations and Leave for the intended organization. Source self-service description is not authorization to remove the current user's access or establish last-owner continuity.

For FPT/GHEC, leaving does not update the organization's stored billing information. A person responsible for payment must arrange another owner or billing manager to update the payment method; removing membership is not proof of billing handoff or stopped charges.

For FPT/GHEC, leaving every organization in an enterprise may automatically remove enterprise membership, but the guide explicitly allows it not to happen and points to the enterprise-leave procedure. Organization departure cannot certify enterprise departure.

The request procedure is FPT/GHEC, not GHES. Organization members can request owner approval; outside collaborators can do so only when integration access requests are enabled. Eligibility is not actual owner approval or app access.

Requesting organization approval requires prior personal-account authorization of the OAuth app. Personal authorization and organization approval are separate state-changing permissions; neither is performed or silently granted by this source review.

The resolved flow uses Settings, Integrations, Applications, Authorized OAuth Apps, selects an app, Request access for the organization, reviews information and Request approval from owners. Request submission is not approval, successful resource access or least-privilege verification.

Organization members can view the People list and filter by Role across FPT/GHES/GHEC. A role-filtered listing is not an exhaustive access census; hidden, inherited or resource-specific access requires its own evidence.

FPT directs enterprise-cloud organizations to the GHEC guide for enterprise owners; GHES/GHEC render the Enterprise permissions, Enterprise owners view. Enterprise owners have differing organization-resource access according to their organization role, not uniform access inferred from enterprise title.

The roles and enterprise-administrator links provide further scope, not evidence that an actor has a current owner role or authority to change policies. Source navigation and screenshots are not executed role observations.
